plan: [In a 3‑bidder third‑price auction the winner pays the minimum of the other two bids, so your payment doesn't depend on your own bid (only on winning). Assuming opponents bid their values (uniform 0–49), expected profit is maximized by bidding high enough to win whenever opponents are low. The optimum (2v) exceeds 49, so bidding at least 49 secures the win and yields expected profit 35−49/3≈$18.67. I will bid 49.]

[With no history and independent values, assume symmetric strategies. For three bidders, best-response analysis yields b* = 2v: bidding twice your value is a symmetric equilibrium. Expected payment ≈ b/3 and win probability (v/49)^2, giving positive expected payoff. Therefore bid 2 * 32 = 64.0 (rounded to $0.1).]

[One round, value v=48. In a 3-bidder third-price auction the winner pays the lowest bid, so raising my bid increases win probability while payment depends on opponents' lower bid. With no history, assume opponents' bids are distributed across the range. Maximizing expected payoff (prob(win) * (v − E[min opponent bid | win])) gives a boundary optimum at b = min(2v,49). For v=48 this yields b=49. So bid the top permissible value to maximize win probability and expected surplus.]
